name: Hydroponics & Controlled-Environment Agriculture

objectives.text: Identify the things a plant needs to grow, including light, water, air, and nutrients, and recognize that some plants can grow in water without soil
Observe and record the growth of seedlings grown in water and seedlings grown in soil over several weeks
Explain how a plant grown in water still gets the nutrients it needs from minerals dissolved in the water
Describe how a greenhouse traps heat and protects plants so crops can be grown outside their normal season
Identify common soilless growing media such as rockwool, perlite, coco coir, and expanded clay pebbles and explain how they support plant roots
Diagram a simple hydroponic system and label its parts, including the reservoir, pump, air stone, and growing tray
Construct and maintain a simple passive hydroponic system, such as a Kratky jar, to grow a leafy crop
Explain how grow lights, light color, and photoperiod affect the growth of plants raised indoors
Describe how an aquaponic system links fish and plants through the nitrogen cycle
Explain how active and passive hydroponic systems deliver water, nutrients, and oxygen to plant roots

Compare and contrast hydroponic and aquaponic production systems such as nutrient film technique, deep water culture, ebb and flow, drip, and aeroponics in terms of design, crop suitability, and management
Compare soilless growing media by water-holding capacity, air porosity, pH, and reusability to select a medium for a specific crop
Measure and adjust the pH and electrical conductivity of a nutrient solution using calibrated meters
Analyze how nutrient solution concentration, pH, dissolved oxygen, and water temperature affect nutrient uptake and plant growth in a hydroponic system
Calculate and mix a nutrient solution from fertilizer concentrates for a specific crop and growth stage
Diagnose nutrient deficiency and toxicity symptoms in hydroponic crops and determine corrective actions
Propagate seedlings or cuttings and transplant them into a hydroponic system following current industry practices

Explain how greenhouse environmental controls such as heating, ventilation, evaporative cooling, shade, humidity control, and carbon dioxide enrichment regulate crop germination, growth, and development
Calculate daily light integral and evaluate supplemental lighting options such as LED and high-pressure sodium fixtures for a controlled-environment crop
Apply integrated pest management practices, including sanitation, scouting, and biological controls, to manage pests and diseases in a greenhouse or indoor farm
Recommend a hydroponic or aquaponic system for a given crop, site, and budget and justify the choice
Maintain production records for a hydroponic enterprise and analyze yield, input costs, and profitability
Evaluate the economic and environmental tradeoffs of controlled-environment agriculture, including energy use, water efficiency, and local food production in vertical farms
Design and manage a controlled-environment production system for a supervised agricultural experience, including a nutrient management plan, lighting, climate control, and crop schedule

changes: Kept and reworded all six original objectives, moving the system comparison to grade 9 and broadening it to include aquaponics so it carries AFNR standards. Added foundational objectives on plant needs, water versus soil growth observation, greenhouses, soilless media, grow lights, aquaponics, and passive system construction for the lower grades. Added high school competencies on pH and EC measurement, nutrient solution mixing, deficiency diagnosis, propagation, greenhouse environmental controls, daily light integral and lighting, integrated pest management, system recommendation, enterprise records, and the tradeoffs of controlled-environment agriculture. The grade 12 capstone is now framed as an SAE project. Standards are assigned only at grades 9 to 12.
